cases.Description:
Hi Team,

Can you please check the below issue with the UD Decon Put Away process at Station 9?

Issue 1: Mark Full Option Missing

At Station 9, we are performing User Directed (UD) Put Away for Decons.
The station is using the newer TTP UI.
Unlike Station 10, the "Mark Full" option is not available at Station 9.
This creates an operational challenge because users are unable to put away all items from a tote into a bin using the Mark Full functionality.
At Station 10, which is running the older GTP UI, the Mark Full option is available and functioning correctly for the same UD Decon Put Away process.

Issue 2: Quantity Change Not Reflected

At Station 9, when the user changes the put away quantity (for example from 1 to 2) before confirming the slot, the system still processes and displays that only 1 quantity was put away.
A video and screenshot have been attached demonstrating the behavior.

Request:

Please verify why the Mark Full option is not available on Station 9.
Please investigate the quantity update issue where the entered quantity is not being reflected correctly after confirmation.
Kindly confirm whether this is an expected behavior, configuration issue, or application defect.

Station Affected: Station 9

Attachments: Video and screenshot demonstrating both issues.

cases.Description:
Hi Team,

*Reported Issue:  *Attached is a video and an excel file with Data with the
test cases highlighted in yellow. This video shows what is happening, when
two small tickets are inducted for the same ranger then there is a delay,
then the ranger circles back into the induct queue. And there is no record
of the scan attempt.

the video was recorded at 1352 EST on June 24th 2026
 on ranger 7018


when one of these Dillard's cases with two labels are inducted 1 at a time
it sorts it just fine fyi, it is just when there is one of these Dillard's
with two labels, with any other small ticket sort

I think the issue stems from the 1-4 sorting rules originally set up as
these cases weren't part of the implementation data we had at that time.

the cases causing the issues do fall under Rule 2 AND Rule 3



Rule1: Accept any code beginning with 1Z, max 256 chars
Rule2: Accept any 34-character code beginning with 1 or 96
Rule3: Accept any 20-digit numeric code beginning with 00008
Rule4: Accept any 10-digit numeric code

OLD Cases: 258941


Thanks,
Raushan Kumar

closedAlerts.subject: Prod Platform Core H&M Canada – Rapid Disk Utilization Due to Tomcat Log Growth
closedAlerts.Description:
**Issue:**

While monitoring the disk utilization for **prod-platform-core – H&M Canada**, we observed continuous growth in the `/opt` partition due to rapid generation of Tomcat logs.

**Findings:**

* `/opt/tomcat/logs` was identified as the major contributor to disk utilization.
* At **10:30 AM**, Tomcat logs were approximately **126 GB**.
* Currently, Tomcat logs have increased to approximately **131 GB**, an increase of around **5 GB**.
* Total `/opt/tomcat` size increased from **133 GB to 137 GB**.
* Current `/opt` partition utilization is around **87%**.
* `catalina.out` is growing rapidly, with multiple rotated `catalina.out.*` files being generated.
* We observed repeated `NoClassDefFoundError` for `SubscriberPayloadValidator`, followed by HTTP 500 responses and retry attempts.
* Approximately **210 occurrences** of this error were observed in the current `catalina.out`.

**Actions Taken:**

* Performed first-level analysis of disk utilization and Tomcat log growth.
* Identified Tomcat logs as the primary contributor to the increasing disk usage.
* Checked `catalina.out` and rotated log files and identified rapid log generation.
* Identified the repeated `SubscriberPayloadValidator` error as a possible contributor to the excessive log generation.
* Aligned with **TAC, SRE, and Platform teams** for further investigation.
